- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.5) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 2–4% to forecast for next 7 days.  
- Model frequently overpredicts mid-term (14–30d) if recent sentiment is mixed or trending upward; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for 14–21d horizon.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after rising) within 7–10 days, model often fails to correct; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
